Numerically stable softmax and additive log-ratio derivatives

Bastien Chassagnol

2026-07-19

Source: vignettes/softmax-alr-derivatives.qmd

This vignette collects the closed-form derivatives that DeCovarT needs to move between the unconstrained coordinates 𝛒∈ℝJ−1\boldsymbol{\rho}\in\mathbb{R}^{J-1} and the cellular ratios 𝐩∈ΔJ−1\boldsymbol{p}\in\Delta^{J-1}. For every map we give the explicit tensor formula, an efficient base-R implementation (evaluated and checked against numDeriv), and a batched PyTorch counterpart. The naming follows the DeCovarT API: additive_logistic() for 𝛒↦𝐩\boldsymbol{\rho}\mapsto\boldsymbol{p} and additive_log_ratio() for 𝐩↦𝛒\boldsymbol{p}\mapsto\boldsymbol{\rho}.

Log-sum-exp and softmax

The softmax of a score vector 𝐳∈ℝK\boldsymbol{z}\in\mathbb{R}^{K} is evaluated through the log-sum-exp (LSE) to avoid overflow,

si=softmax⁡(𝐳)i=ezi∑kezk=ezi−LSE⁡(𝐳),LSE⁡(𝐳)=m+log⁡∑kezk−m,m=maxkzk.(1) s_i=\operatorname{softmax}(\boldsymbol{z})_i=\frac{e^{z_i}}{\sum_{k}e^{z_k}} =e^{z_i-\operatorname{LSE}(\boldsymbol{z})}, \qquad \operatorname{LSE}(\boldsymbol{z})=m+\log\!\sum_{k}e^{z_k-m}, \quad m=\max_k z_k. \qquad(1)

Softmax Jacobian and Hessian

The softmax Jacobian is the difference between a diagonal and a rank-one term,

∂si∂zj=si(δij−sj),𝐉softmax=diag⁡(𝐬)−𝐬𝐬⊤.(2) \frac{\partial s_i}{\partial z_j}=s_i(\delta_{ij}-s_j), \qquad \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{softmax}}=\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol{s}) -\boldsymbol{s}\boldsymbol{s}^{\top}. \qquad(2)

This matrix also equals the Hessian of the log-sum-exp, ∇2LSE⁡(𝐳)=diag⁡(𝐬)−𝐬𝐬⊤\nabla^2\operatorname{LSE}(\boldsymbol{z})=\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol{s}) -\boldsymbol{s}\boldsymbol{s}^{\top}. Because softmax is vector-valued, its second derivative is a third-order tensor Hijk=∂2si/(∂zj∂zk)H_{ijk}=\partial^2 s_i/(\partial z_j\partial z_k),

Hijk=si[(δij−sj)(δik−sk)−sj(δjk−sk)],(3) H_{ijk}=s_i\bigl[(\delta_{ij}-s_j)(\delta_{ik}-s_k)-s_j(\delta_{jk}-s_k)\bigr], \qquad(3)

which, slice by slice, is the rank-one correction

𝐇(i)=si[(𝐞i−𝐬)(𝐞i−𝐬)⊤−(diag⁡(𝐬)−𝐬𝐬⊤)],(4) \mathbf{H}^{(i)}=s_i\Bigl[(\boldsymbol{e}_i-\boldsymbol{s}) (\boldsymbol{e}_i-\boldsymbol{s})^{\top} -\bigl(\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol{s})-\boldsymbol{s}\boldsymbol{s}^{\top}\bigr) \Bigr], \qquad(4)

with 𝐞i\boldsymbol{e}_i the ii-th canonical basis vector. Listing 3 materialises Eq. 2 and Eq. 4 in O(K2)O(K^2) per slice.

Additive log-ratio coordinates

Let 𝐩=(p1,…,pJ)\boldsymbol{p}=(p_1,\ldots,p_J) be a composition with pj>0p_j>0 and ∑jpj=1\sum_j p_j=1, and take the last part JJ as reference. The additive log-ratio (alr) transform sends the composition to ℝJ−1\mathbb{R}^{J-1},

ρi=log⁡(pipJ),i=1,…,J−1,(5) \rho_i=\log\!\Bigl(\frac{p_i}{p_J}\Bigr),\qquad i=1,\ldots,J-1, \qquad(5)

and its inverse, the additive logistic transform (alr−1\mathrm{alr}^{-1}), pins a reference logit at zero, 𝛒̃=(ρ1,…,ρJ−1,0)\tilde{\boldsymbol{\rho}}=(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_{J-1},0), and applies a softmax,

𝐩=softmax⁡(𝛒̃),pi=eρi1+∑j<Jeρj(i<J),pJ=11+∑j<Jeρj.(6) \boldsymbol{p}=\operatorname{softmax}(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\rho}}), \qquad p_i=\frac{e^{\rho_i}}{1+\sum_{j<J}e^{\rho_j}}\ (i<J), \qquad p_J=\frac{1}{1+\sum_{j<J}e^{\rho_j}}. \qquad(6)

Derivatives of the additive logistic map (𝛒↦𝐩\boldsymbol{\rho}\mapsto\boldsymbol{p})

The additive logistic map is the softmax restricted to the first J−1J-1 inputs, so its Jacobian 𝐉𝛙∈ℳJ×(J−1)\mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}\in\mathcal{M}_{J\times(J-1)} is the softmax Jacobian with the reference column dropped,

∂pi∂ρa=pi(δia−pa),𝐉𝛙=[diag⁡(𝐩)−𝐩𝐩⊤]:,1:(J−1),a=1,…,J−1.(7) \frac{\partial p_i}{\partial\rho_a}=p_i(\delta_{ia}-p_a), \qquad \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}} =\bigl[\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol{p}) -\boldsymbol{p}\boldsymbol{p}^{\top}\bigr]_{:,\,1:(J-1)}, \qquad a=1,\ldots,J-1. \qquad(7)

Its Hessian is a tensor 𝐇𝛙∈ℳJ×(J−1)×(J−1)\mathbf{H}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}\in\mathcal{M}_{J\times(J-1)\times(J-1)}, the softmax Hessian Eq. 4 restricted to the first J−1J-1 input indices,

∂2pi∂ρa∂ρb=pi[(δia−pa)(δib−pb)−pa(δab−pb)],a,b=1,…,J−1.(8) \frac{\partial^2 p_i}{\partial\rho_a\partial\rho_b} =p_i\bigl[(\delta_{ia}-p_a)(\delta_{ib}-p_b)-p_a(\delta_{ab}-p_b)\bigr], \qquad a,b=1,\ldots,J-1. \qquad(8)

Derivatives of the additive log-ratio map (𝐩↦𝛒\boldsymbol{p}\mapsto\boldsymbol{\rho})

Treating 𝐩\boldsymbol{p} as ambient coordinates in ℝJ\mathbb{R}^{J} (admissible tangent directions satisfy ∑idpi=0\sum_i \mathrm{d}p_i=0), the alr Jacobian 𝐉alr∈ℳ(J−1)×J\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{alr}}\in\mathcal{M}_{(J-1)\times J} is sparse,

∂ρi∂pj=δijpi−δjJpJ,𝐉alr=[diag⁡(p1−1,…,pJ−1−1)|−pJ−1𝟏J−1],(9) \frac{\partial\rho_i}{\partial p_j}=\frac{\delta_{ij}}{p_i}-\frac{\delta_{jJ}}{p_J}, \qquad \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{alr}} =\Bigl[\operatorname{diag}\!\bigl(p_1^{-1},\ldots,p_{J-1}^{-1}\bigr) \ \big|\ -p_J^{-1}\boldsymbol{1}_{J-1}\Bigr], \qquad(9)

and its Hessian 𝐇alr∈ℳ(J−1)×J×J\mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{alr}}\in\mathcal{M}_{(J-1)\times J\times J} is diagonal in the last two modes,

∂2ρi∂pj∂pk=−δijδikpi2+δjJδkJpJ2.(10) \frac{\partial^2\rho_i}{\partial p_j\partial p_k} =-\frac{\delta_{ij}\delta_{ik}}{p_i^{2}} +\frac{\delta_{jJ}\delta_{kJ}}{p_J^{2}}. \qquad(10)

Reference implementations

Both transforms are standard in compositional data analysis. In R, the compositions package exposes alr() / alrInv(). In Python, scikit-bio provides skbio.stats.composition.alr() and alr_inv(). DeCovarT’s additive_logistic() and additive_log_ratio() are the same maps with the last part fixed as reference.

Checking the closed forms

The analytic derivatives are validated against Richardson extrapolation in R (Listing 12).
